lessons.culture: The Great Mosque of Sana'a (الجامع الكبير) is one of the oldest mosques in the world, and the old city around it, entered through باب اليمن, is a UNESCO World Heritage site of tall brick tower houses. Visitors take off their shoes at the mosque door, dress modestly and keep away from prayer times, and women cover their hair.

lessons.culture: Sana'a lies high in the mountains, so families travel to Aden, al-Hudayda or al-Mukalla for the sea, mostly in the cooler months when the coast is pleasant. Beaches are family places: families picnic in the shade in the late afternoon, and women who go into the water do so fully and modestly dressed.

dialogue.english: Very tasty, I will take a box. And what is this perfume?

pair.english: I want a souvenir for my family

response.english: I have lots of things, have a look.

pair.english: Do you have good dates?

response.english: Yes, go ahead and taste.

pair.english: What is this perfume?

response.english: This is natural oud.

pair.english: Is this handmade?

response.english: Yes, handmade in Sana'a.

pair.arabic: تِنَزِّل لِي فِي السِّعْر لَوْ شَلَّيْت ثِنْتَيْن؟
pair.transliteration: tinazzil li fi s-si3r law shallayt thintayn?
pair.english: Will you give me a lower price if I take two?

response.english: OK, I will take a little off for you.

lessons.culture: Sana'a's old market, سوق الملح, is where people buy Yemeni gifts: honey from Hadramawt, coffee beans, agate (عقيق) rings, incense and the spice mix حويج. Bargaining is polite and unhurried: you ask once for a better price, and the seller often lets you taste or adds something small.

exercises.prompt: The seller asks: "إيش تشتي؟" Say you want a prayer rug.
exercises.tip: "إيش تشتي؟" is "what do you want?" in Sana'a.

exercises.prompt: You ask: "إيش هذا العطر؟" Answer as the seller: this is natural oud.
Complete: "أشتي علبة _____ هدية." (I want a box of spices as a gift.)
exercises.tip: "حويج" is the Yemeni word for spices and the spice mix.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "تقدر _____ هدية؟" (Can you wrap it as a gift?)
Translate: "I want a silk scarf for my sister."
Translate: "Is this handmade?"

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; ask "هذا شغل يد؟".

exercises.prompt: Which one asks for a lower price if you take two?
exercises.answer: تِنَزِّل لِي فِي السِّعْر لَوْ شَلَّيْت ثِنْتَيْن؟
accepted: تِنَزِّل لِي فِي السِّعْر لَوْ شَلَّيْت ثِنْتَيْن؟
تنزل لي في السعر لو شليت ثنتين؟
tinazzil li fi s-si3r law shallayt thintayn
options: تِنَزِّل لِي فِي السِّعْر لَوْ شَلَّيْت ثِنْتَيْن؟

exercises.prompt: Which one means "This is a gift for my mother, I hope she likes it"?
exercises.answer: هَذِي هَدِيَّة لِأُمِّي، إِن شَاء الله تِعْجِبْهَا
accepted: هَذِي هَدِيَّة لِأُمِّي، إِن شَاء الله تِعْجِبْهَا
هذي هدية لأمي، إن شاء الله تعجبها
haadhi hadiyya li-ummi, in shaa2 allaah ti3jibha
options: هَذِي هَدِيَّة لِأُمِّي، إِن شَاء الله تِعْجِبْهَا

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "This wooden box is beautiful."
Put the words in order: "I want a small bottle of oud oil."

reply.english: I will travel to Aden, to the sea.
OK, I will send them now.
It was really lovely, and we enjoyed ourselves.
Thank God for your safe return.

dialogue.speaker: عمر
dialogue.arabic: ما شاء الله! تشلّ الكاميرا معك؟
dialogue.transliteration: maa shaa2 allaah! tishill al-kaamira ma3ak?
dialogue.english: Ma sha Allah! Are you taking your camera?

dialogue.speaker: عمر
dialogue.english: Welcome, Khalid! You are back?

dialogue.speaker: خالد
dialogue.arabic: ابسر الصور، البحر كان هادي قوي.
dialogue.transliteration: ibsir aS-Suwar, al-ba7r kaan haadi gawi.
dialogue.english: Look at the photos, the sea was very calm.

pair.english: Where are you going this holiday?

response.english: I will travel to Aden, to the sea.

pair.english: How long does your holiday last?

response.english: Two weeks.

pair.english: Can you take a photo of us?

response.english: Sure, stand over there.

pair.english: Send me the photos on my phone

response.english: OK, I will send them now.

pair.english: How was your trip?

response.english: It was really lovely, and we enjoyed ourselves.

lessons.culture: Yemeni families mostly travel in the Eid holidays and the long summer school break, often to relatives in their home village or to the coast at Aden or al-Mukalla. A traveller is welcomed back with الحمد لله على السلامة, and it is polite to ask before photographing anyone, especially women.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "وين عتسافر هذي الإجازة؟" Say you will travel to Aden, to the sea.
You say: "رجعنا سالمين، الحمد لله." What does your friend answer?
exercises.tip: This welcome-back phrase is shared by every dialect.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "البحر هادي _____." (The sea is very calm.)
Complete: "ارسل لي الصور على _____." (Send me the photos on my phone.)
Translate: "We are travelling with the whole family."

too_formal.feedback: "سـ" is the written future; in Sana'a "we will" takes "شا".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Can you take a photo of us?" (to a man)
Which one means "What a beautiful view!"?
Which one means "We booked a house near the beach"?
Put the words in order: "The sunset is beautiful here."
Put the words in order: "How was your trip?"

challenge.title: احْجِز رِحْلَة وحُلّ مُشْكِلَة
challenge.instructions: اعْمِل حِوار قَصِير: احْجِز غُرْفَة بِفِندَق أَوْ تَذْكِرَة سَفَر، وبَعْدِيْن ظَهِرِت مُشْكِلَة (تأْخِير، شِنْطَة ضايِعَة، أَو الطَّيَّارَة فاتِتَك) وَحِكِ كَيْف حَلَّيْتَها.
required_elements: طَلَب حِجْز أَوْ تَذْكِرَة بِجُمْلَة كامِلَة

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُم، أَشْتِي أَحْجِز تَذْكِرَة لِحَلِب
dialogue.english: Hello, I want to book a ticket to Aleppo.

dialogue.speaker: مُوَظَّف
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُم السَّلام، رايِح بَس وِلاّ رايِح جاي؟
dialogue.transliteration: w 3alaykum s-salaam, rayyi7 bas willa rayyi7 jaay?
dialogue.english: One-way or round trip?

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.english: Round trip, how much?

dialogue.speaker: مُوَظَّف
dialogue.arabic: أَرْبَعِمِيَّة رِيال، الْبَاص يِطْلَع السَّاعَة تِسْعَة
dialogue.transliteration: arba3imiyya riyal, l-baaS yiTla3 s-saa3a tis3a
dialogue.english: Four hundred riyals, the bus leaves at nine.

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.arabic: لِلأَسَف فاتنِي الْبَاص، فِيه بَاص ثانِي؟
dialogue.transliteration: lal2asaf faatni l-baaS, fiih baaS thaani?
dialogue.english: I missed the bus, is there another one?

dialogue.speaker: مُوَظَّف
dialogue.english: Yes, there's a bus in two hours.

dialogue.speaker: مُحَمَّد
dialogue.english: Thank God, thanks a lot.
